text: To confer something is to give or grant it, usually a benefit, honor or power. It can also mean to hold a discussion with someone, as in conferring with a lawyer. Here  it means that powerful AI would hand its builders a huge edge over rival countries, which is why scary warnings can make the technology look even more valuable.

Degradation is a gradual decline in quality, condition or value. Environmental degradation means nature getting worse step by step: soil wearing out, water getting dirty, forests shrinking. In the article it is one of several slow-moving problems that, together, can bring a society down.

To buffer is to cushion or protect something from a shock, like a bumper softening a crash. As a noun, a buffer is the cushion itself. Here  Australia's remoteness softens the blow from some global disasters, since trouble has a harder time reaching an island far from everyone else.

In math, a singularity is a point where a quantity shoots off toward infinity and the formula stops making sense. In AI talk it means the moment machines start improving themselves faster than people can follow.
A crunch is a sudden, severe squeeze or crisis. Here it means the point at which the world would become too crowded to support its people.
Inevitable means certain to happen and impossible to avoid. The scientists believed population growth made the crunch unavoidable, and they turned out to be wrong.
To squash is to crush something by pressing it flat. The joke in the prediction is that the planet would be so packed that people would press each other to death.
Reassuringly means in a way that makes you feel calmer. A spacious room at a talk about overcrowding is a gentle irony.
Spacious means having plenty of room. It is the opposite of the crowded world the 1960 paper predicted.
To assess is to carefully judge the size, quality or importance of something. The researchers gathered to weigh up how likely various threats are.
Civilisation is the complex society humans build, with cities, governments, farming and trade. The conference asked whether ours will last.
Superintelligent describes a mind far smarter than any human. It is a feature of the most dramatic AI worries.
Antibiotic resistance is when germs evolve to survive the drugs that used to kill them, making ordinary infections harder to treat. It is listed as a real threat to humanity.
An existential risk is a danger big enough to wipe out humanity or permanently wreck its future. It is the field Dr Kemp studies.
A magazine founded by scientists who built the first atomic bombs. It runs the Doomsday Clock, a symbol of how close humanity is to disaster, with midnight meaning catastrophe.
A symbolic clock where midnight stands for global catastrophe. Moving the hand closer is a way to warn that dangers are growing.
Sandwich boards are signs worn on the front and back of a person, like a human billboard. The cartoon picture is a ragged man announcing that the end is nigh.
To go mainstream is to move from the fringe into ordinary, widely accepted conversation. Doomsday talk is no longer just for cranks.
To eye something up is to look at it with interest, often thinking of buying or taking it. The billionaires are shopping for hideouts.
Bunkers are strong underground shelters built to survive attacks or disasters. Wealthy people are buying luxurious versions.
Pessimistic means expecting the worst. Dr Kemp's view of humanity's long-term chances is gloomy.
Fundamentally means at the deepest, most basic level. He means a deep rebuild of society, not a few tweaks.
Autonomously means on its own, without human control. In the AI story, machines would improve themselves with no help from people.
Mass surveillance is watching or tracking large numbers of ordinary people, such as through cameras and data. AI could make it far cheaper and more thorough.
Wealth inequality is the gap between how much the richest and everyone else own. Dr Kemp fears AI could widen it.
Headline-grabbing means dramatic enough to get news coverage. Robot uprisings fit; slow problems like inequality do not.
Institutions are the lasting organisations and rules of a society, such as governments, courts and banks. Collapse happens when these are weakened.
Resilience is the ability to recover from shocks and keep going. A society with little resilience breaks under pressure.
The western half of the Roman Empire, which fell in 476AD. It is used as an example of a collapse that looked sudden but had centuries of causes.
Turmoil is a state of confusion, upheaval and unrest. Rome suffered centuries of it before its fall.
To exhaust resources is to use them up completely. A society that runs out of farmland, water or energy is in trouble.
Best-positioned means in the most favourable situation to cope. Australia ranked first in the analysis.
Infrastructure is the basic systems a society runs on, like roads, power grids and ports.
Vulnerable means easily harmed. A country safe from one danger may still be exposed to another.
A saying meaning there is no safe refuge. Dr Kemp means that modern food, medicine and energy systems are so linked that no hideout escapes a collapse.
To outwit is to beat someone through cleverness. The fear is that AI could out-think the people who control it.
To cripple is to damage something so badly that it cannot work properly. Here it describes AI disabling vital systems like power grids.
A strategic advantage is a lasting edge over rivals in competition or conflict. Countries want it from AI.
Compelling means so convincing that it is hard to resist. A scary forecast makes the investment case stronger.
Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by pollution from burning coal and oil, which harmed forests and lakes. International deals to cut the pollution largely fixed it.
The ozone layer is a thin shield of gas high in the sky that blocks harmful ultraviolet light. A global ban on certain chemicals helped it recover.
To curb is to hold something in check or reduce it. Countries curbed pollution after the warnings.
Lockdowns were rules during the pandemic that kept people at home to slow the spread of disease.
